course_profile.one_sentence_summary: A foundational university mathematics course covering matrices, linear systems, vector algebra, analytic geometry, and linear spaces.
course_profile.short_summary: This course provides essential mathematical knowledge for software engineering students. It covers matrix operations, determinants, solving systems of linear equations via the Gaussian method, vector dot and cross products, equations of lines and planes, and characteristics of 2nd-order curves and surfaces. Advanced topics include linear spaces, linear operators, eigenvectors, and quadratic forms.

theoretical_understanding: Understand the properties of matrices and determinants.
Understand the conditions for solvability of systems of linear algebraic equations (Kronecker-Capelli theorem).
Understand the geometric interpretation of dot, cross, and mixed vector products.
Understand the theoretical basis of linear spaces, basis vectors, and linear independence.
Understand the characteristics of second-order curves (ellipse, parabola, hyperbola) and surfaces.
practical_implementation: Perform arithmetic operations on matrices and calculate inverse matrices.
Solve systems of linear equations using Gaussian elimination and Cramer's methods.
Calculate scalar, vector, and mixed products of vectors using coordinates.
Formulate equations for lines and planes in various spatial configurations.
Find eigenvalues and eigenvectors of linear operators.
analysis_validation: Determine the rank of a matrix.
Analyze the linear dependence or independence of a system of vectors.
Investigate the mutual positioning of straight lines and planes in space.
Reduce quadratic forms to their canonical form and determine their definiteness.

implementation_tasks: Solving matrix equations and finding inverse matrices
Deriving equations for analytical geometry shapes
Diagonalizing operators and working with quadratic forms
engineering_practices: Mathematical modeling of physical and mechanical problems

curricular_relations.reason: High school algebra is explicitly stated as the foundational prerequisite for this course.
Matrix operations and determinants are required to represent and solve systems of linear equations.
High school geometry provides the spatial understanding necessary for vector algebra.
Vector operations (dot, cross products) are used to derive equations for lines, planes, and normal vectors in analytical geometry.

what_student_can_understand: The mathematical foundations of linear spaces, transformations, and coordinate systems.
The theoretical mechanics behind 2D and 3D geometric intersections and surface modeling.
what_student_can_build: Mathematical models representing lines, planes, and quadratic curves.
Solutions for complex linear systems using algorithmic matrix operations.
what_student_can_apply: Vector calculus for physics and mechanics problems.
Matrix operations applicable to computer graphics and software engineering algorithms.
